chunks: On their bodies will be garments of the finest green silk and brocade, and they will be adorned with bracelets of silver; and their Lord will give them a purest draught to drink.
ai.seo_question: What are the specific rewards and attire described for the righteous in Paradise in this Quranic verse?
ai.summary: This verse from Surah Al--Insan (76:22) depicts the eternal abode of the righteous, where green silk (dibaj) and brocade (istabraq) signify nobility and purity, distinct from the gold and silk reserved for women or general luxury. Shia exegesis, such as in Al-Mizan, emphasizes that the 'pure drink' (sharabun tahur) refers to wine free from intoxication's negative effects, symbolizing spiritual clarity and divine proximity. The attire and drink together illustrate the harmonious union of physical comfort and spiritual elevation in Jannah.
